title: E-Invoice Onboarding Checklist for Accounting Teams
summary: Follow this e-invoice onboarding checklist to prepare your accounting team, verify GST details, configure systems, and ensure smooth compliance.
body_markdown:
The easier it is for an accounting group to manage e-invoicing, the better prepared they will be to get it done when the time comes. The E-Invoice[Onboarding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Onboarding) **** Checklist is a predefined list that can be used to verify and validate details such as GSTIN, Customer details, HSN or SAC code, Tax rates, Invoice numbering, Portal access, and Integration settings while generating e-invoices. It also provides a uniform error-handling process, IRN, QR code, cancellation, and a timely reporting process for the team.


## **What Is E-Invoice Onboarding?**


The process of preparing an accounting team and their billing system to generate and report e-invoices properly is known as E-invoice onboarding. It also covers checking whether the business and other relevant GSTINs are covered or not.


## **What is the Need for an E-Invoice Onboarding Checklist for Accounting Teams?**


Most of the errors in E-invoices happen before an invoice is received by the IRP. Mismatches in GSTIN, invalid HSN codes, wrong taxable values, wrong tax rates, duplicate invoice details, lack of buyer information, etc., can cause validation failures or may cause issues for reconciliation.


‍ **Key benefits**


- Orderly invoices from different users and branches.
- Fewer validation failures and rejected requests.
- More control when creating invoices.
- Define clear responsibilities for generating e-invoices.
- Better matching of billing records with GST records.
- Quickly identify when an invoice fails with no hassle.


## **E-Invoice Onboarding Checklist for Accounting Teams**


### **1. Confirm E-Invoice Applicability**


First, verify the aggregate annual turnover of the business and whether the business has the relevant GSTIN enabled for e-invoicing. The turnover level for determining the threshold is taken as per GST registration with the same PAN. Businesses should also check to see if there is any particular exemption that applies to the business before starting implementation.


### **2. Ensure IRP Access and User Security**


After the applicability, check access to the e-invoice portal and ensure that the required activities can be carried out by the required users. Companies with an integrated billing system also need to make sure that the necessary API or GSP setup is in place and that their credentials are not distributed to several employees.


### **3. Clean and Verify Master Data**


- Master Data
- What to Check
- Supplier GSTIN
- Correct GSTIN and legal name
- Customer GSTIN
- Valid GSTIN and registered name
- HSN/SAC
- Correct code and description
- Tax rates
- Applicable CGST, SGST, IGST and cess
- Invoice series
- Unique and correctly set up
- Addresses
- Billing and shipping details
- Unit of Measure
- Correct UQC
- Product information
- Description, amount, and value for tax purpose


‍ **Also Read:**[E-invoice for credit notes and debit notes](https://getswipe.in/blog/article/e-invoice-credit-notes-debit-notes-reporting-workflow)


### **4. Set up Invoice Numbering and Formats**


Before going live, accounting teams should examine the invoice prefixes, numbering sequences, document types, and branch-wise series. The billing system should provide consistent invoice numbers to make sure that users don't create duplicate or conflicting invoice numbers.


### **5. Link the E-Invoice System to the Billing Software.**


If the business has billing or accounting software, do the software integration before production use. The team needs to confirm the connection, authentication information, GSTIN mapping, API configuration, and response handling.


### **6. Test Transactions**


Don't skip the configuration phase and jump into full production. Develop test invoices and confirm that the system returns the valid information, accepts the IRN, produces the QR code, and updates the status of the invoice successfully.


### **7. Write an Error-Handling SOP**


All the accounting teams must understand what to do when a request for an e-invoice fails. The SOP may involve checking the error message, determining the wrong field, fixing the source invoice, reattempting only when the previous request status is confirmed, and recording the final IRN.


## **To help you get the process of E-Invoice Onboarding started quickly.**


- To check the applicability of e-invoice.
- Verification of GSTIN and access to the portal.
- MFA and user access are set up.
- GSTINs of customers & suppliers are checked.
- The review of HSN/SAC and UQC data is carried out.
- Checks for correct tax rate and invoice numbering.
- Software testing is performed for billing software.
- Invoices can be generated successfully for tests.
- The handling of IRN and QR code is confirmed.
- Documentation of error-handling procedures.
- E-invoice reconciliation is assigned.
- Deadlines for reporting are monitored.


‍ **Also Read:**[E-invoice business continuity plan](https://getswipe.in/blog/article/e-invoice-business-continuity-plan)


## **How Billing Software Facilitates E-Invoice Onboarding**


Manual work can be minimized during the onboarding process with a connected billing system. Accounting teams can simply create an invoice from the typical billing process and send the necessary information through integrated e-invoicing tools.


## **Conclusion**


An E-Invoice Onboarding Checklist is an excellent resource for accounting teams to transition from manual or disjointed invoicing to a more structured and repeatable e-invoicing process. The critical activities are: Applicability, Portal Access, Cleaning of Master Data, Invoice Numbering Configuration, Billing Software Connection, Transaction Testing, Error Handling Documentation, and Invoices reporting reconciliation.


## **FAQs**


### **1. What exactly is an e-invoice onboarding checklist?**


An e-invoice onboarding checklist is a series of actions that can be used to introduce an accounting team and their billing system to e-invoicing.


### **2. What should be checked before producing an e-invoice?**


Teams should confirm the GSTIN, invoice number, invoice date, HSN/SAC Codes, tax rates, taxable values, address, quantity, UQC, and other relevant details of the invoice with the supplier and/or the customer before submitting.


### **3. Does software integration need to be done for e-Invoicing?**


While software integration isn't the only method of creating an e-invoice, integrated billing software can help to minimize manual data entry and simplify e-invoice management.


### **4. If an e-invoice is rejected, what would happen?**


The accounting team should then check the error that is returned by the IRP, identify what's wrong with the information in the source invoice/datasheet, and correct the source invoice/datasheet.


### **5. How to avoid generating duplicate e-invoices?**


If a response is delayed, teams should not repeatedly attempt to submit the response. Before they can do anything else, they should first look at the status of the invoice and check the IRN as soon as it is generated.


### **6. Will the onboarding of e-invoice need to be repeated with every employee?**


The overall system configuration does not need to be rebuilt for all employees, but the relevant employee(s) who are responsible for e-invoicing should receive suitable training and access to the system according to their function.
